previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, pancreas and kidney transplants, end-stage renal disease, and chronic heart failure was admitted for shortness of breath and weakness. She presented with progressive dyspnea, orthopnea, and volume overload, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. Initial evaluation revealed pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and anemia. She underwent hemodialysis, which improved her respiratory status. Due to recurrent hypotension during dialysis, midodrine was initiated to support blood pressure and facilitate fluid removal. Warfarin was held in preparation for an upcoming peritoneal dialysis catheter placement. She received two units of packed red blood cells for anemia and was transitioned to extended care for recovery. Discharge planning included daily weight monitoring, continuation of immunosuppressive and cardiac medications, and readmission for anticoagulation management post-procedure.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure

Discharge Instructions:
Weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs.
Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication.  Please take any 
new medications as prescribed.
Please take the prescribed analgesic medications as needed.  You 
may not drive or heavy machinery while taking narcotic analgesic 
medications.  You may also take acetaminophen (Tylenol) as 
directed, but do not exceed 4000 mg in one day.
Please get plenty of rest, continue to walk several times per 
day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids.  Avoid strenuous 
physical activity and refrain from heavy lifting greater than 
10lbs., until you follow-up with your surgeon, who will instruct 
you further regarding activity restrictions.  Please also 
follow-up with your primary care physician.
Incision Care:
*Please call your surgeon or go to the emergency department if 
you have increased pain, swelling, redness, or drainage from the 
incision site.
*Avoid swimming and baths until cleared by your surgeon.
*You may shower and wash incisions with a mild soap and warm 
water.  Gently pat the area dry.
